subject: storytime
title: The Frog Prince
about: The Brothers Grimm's tale of a princess who promises a frog her friendship if he fetches her golden ball from the well, then has to be reminded by her father the king that a promise is a promise; in the morning the frog turns out to be a prince. First graders enjoy the splash, the knock at the door and the frog at the dinner table, and the story ends with its lesson said plainly: keep your promises. This gentle retelling, without the thrown frog of some versions, is a public-domain story in first-grade words, five pages long.
tip: Ask what the princess promised the frog, and what the king said when she did not want to keep it.

book.author: the Brothers Grimm (retold)
book.source: public domain, retold in first-grade words
book.blurb: A golden ball, a deep well, and a promise to keep.

passage.text:
Once there was a princess.
She had a golden ball.
It was her best toy.
Every day she played by a deep well.
She tossed the ball up high.
One day she missed it.
Splash!
The ball fell into the well.
"Oh no!" cried the princess.
"My ball is gone!"
She sat by the well and cried.
***
"I can get it," said a voice.
It was a big green frog.
"But first you must promise," said the frog.
"Be my friend."
"Let me eat from your plate."
"Let me sleep on your pillow."
"Yes, yes, I promise!" said the princess.
The frog dove down and got the ball.
The princess grabbed it and ran home.
She forgot all about the frog.
***
That night, the princess sat down to eat.
Hop, hop, hop!
Something came up the steps.
Knock, knock!
"Princess! Princess! You made a promise!"
It was the frog.
The princess did not want to let him in.
"What is this?" asked the king.
She told him about the promise.
"A promise is a promise," said the king.
"Let him in."
***
So the frog sat at the table.
"Push your plate closer," said the frog.
He ate from her golden plate.
"Now take me to bed," said the frog.
He slept on her soft pillow.
The princess did not like it one bit.
But a promise is a promise.
So she kept it.
***
In the morning, the frog was gone.
A kind prince stood there instead.
"I was the frog," he said.
"Someone put a spell on me."
"You kept your promise."
"Now the spell is broken!"
The princess smiled.
From then on, they were the best of friends.
If you make a promise, keep it.

cards.note: She tossed it up high every day, and one day she missed: splash.

cards.q: Who got the ball back for the princess?
cards.note: A big green frog in the well offered to dive for it, for a promise.
First her plate, then her pillow: the two things the frog asked for.

cards.q: Who said, 'A promise is a promise'?
cards.note: Her father the king would not let her wriggle out of it.

cards.q: What happened first in the story?
cards.note: The golden ball splashes into the deep well; everything else follows from that.

cards.q: What happened at the end of the story?
cards.note: The frog was a prince under a spell, and her kept promise broke it.

cards.q: How did the princess feel when the ball fell in?
cards.note: She sat by the well and cried; ask how she felt when the frog offered to help.
She did not want to, but she kept her word, and that is what broke the spell.

cards.q: In the story, what is a 'well'?
cards.note: A well is a deep hole dug down to water; a dropped ball is very hard to get back.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: He reads the three words himself; only one of them is in the story.
